title: Certificates
subtitle: HTTPS certificate of each node's web interface: source, checks, renewal
replicationNote: Replication certificates (internal CA and node certificates) stay separate: their expiry raises alerts, they are never replaced here.

sourceHelp.self_signed: The certificate made at install, or a new one made here. Browsers warn until they trust it.
sourceHelp.manual: A certificate you upload: signed from a request made on the node, or certificate, chain and key. No automatic renewal: the expiry alert reminds you.
sourceHelp.acme: Let's Encrypt, a private ACME server (step-ca, UCM) or any ACME URL. The node makes its key, proves its names and renews when a third of the lifetime is left.
sourceHelp.ucm: UCM signs a request made on the node through its API. Renewed before the end (settings: ucm_renew_days).
sourceHelp.inherit: Follow the source set for all nodes.

node.pendingRequest: A request made on this node waits for its signed certificate.

cluster.title: All nodes
cluster.help: One ACME or UCM setting for several nodes: each node makes its own key and requests its own certificate for its own names. Nodes enrolled later follow it.
cluster.applies: Applies to {{nodes}}; each node renews on its own schedule.
cluster.everyNode: every node, including nodes enrolled later
cluster.thresholds: Expiry alerts: warning {{warning}} days, critical {{critical}} days before (Settings).
cluster.clearTitle: Remove the setting for all nodes?
cluster.clearBody: The nodes keep their current certificate and stop renewing it until they get a source of their own.

selfSigned.title: New self-signed certificate on {{node}}?
selfSigned.body: A new key and a ten-year self-signed certificate replace the current one. Browsers will warn until they trust it.

dns01.title: DNS-01 setup
dns01.nothing: The ddi-acme key and its grants are already in place.
dns01.manual: Zones in your own named.conf files: add these grants to their update-policy by hand.
dns01.delegation: Public DNS host: create these CNAME records to delegate the challenges.
dns01.unserved: No zone of this node holds {{names}}: use a DNS provider or a CNAME delegation.

source.applyAll: Save and request on every node
source.title: Source of {{node}}
source.allNodesHelp: Nodes enrolled later follow this setting too
source.namesHelp: Besides the node name and the host of its web URL
source.clusterModeHelp: A load balancer fronts the nodes: every certificate carries the cluster name

acme.eabHelp: External account binding, when the server asks for it
acme.trustRoot: Trust root of the ACME server
acme.trustRootHelp: PEM certificate used to reach a private server; added to the system store
acme.httpHelp: The ACME server connects to port 80: forward it to this port, or route /.well-known/acme-challenge/ to it.

dnsMethods.pelagos: Pelagos, in a zone it serves (key ddi-acme)

acme.dnsServerHelp: Empty: this node's BIND. host[:port] of the primary otherwise
acme.delegationHelp: Zone served by Pelagos that _acme-challenge CNAMEs point to

ucm.trustRootHelp: PEM certificate used to reach UCM when its own is not publicly trusted
ucm.caIdHelp: Test the connection to pick from the list
ucm.revokeOldHelp: After the switch; renewal runs {{days}} days before the end

request.pending: Request for {{names}} made on {{when}}: have it signed, then paste the certificate below.
request.help: The node makes a key that never leaves it and a request (CSR) you have signed by any CA.

upload.title: Certificate of {{node}}

modes.request: Signed certificate for the request made on the node

upload.keyHelp: Written 0600 on the node, never shown again nor written to the audit log
upload.alsoHelp: Only when the certificate covers their names; the key goes encrypted through replication.

key.missing: no private key: give the key or use the request made on the node
key.mismatch: the private key does not match the certificate
key.ok: the private key matches the certificate

dates.not_yet: the certificate is not valid yet
dates.soon: the certificate expires within a week

usage.no_server_auth: the certificate does not allow server authentication
usage.ca: the certificate is a CA certificate, not a server one

chain.ok: the chain is complete and in order
chain.reordered: the chain was given out of order: it is installed in order
chain.incomplete: the chain is incomplete: the issuer {{issuer}} is missing

chain_extra.extra: {{count}} certificates are not part of the chain and are left out

trust.self_signed: self-signed: browsers will warn until they trust it
trust.system: the issuer is trusted by the system
trust.own_root: the issuer is trusted through the root you gave, not by the system
trust.unknown: the issuer is not recognized by the system
